domain.name: adi_flex
domain.one_line: Periodic-review inventory with advance demand information and flexible delivery: joint ordering and allocation under demand crossover (Wang & Toktay 2008, Mgmt Sci 54(4), section 4).

state_variables.name: period
state_variables.desc: current period i; horizon ends when period == n_periods

state_variables.name: inventory
state_variables.desc: net inventory x_i at the start of the period; negative = overdue demand backlogged

state_variables.name: due_now
state_variables.desc: v_i^i — unsatisfied advance demand due by the current period (not yet overdue)

state_variables.name: due_next
state_variables.desc: v_i^(i+1) — unsatisfied advance demand due by the next period

info_fields.name: demand_now
info_fields.desc: d_i^i — demand arriving this period, due this period

info_fields.name: demand_next
info_fields.desc: d_i^(i+1) — arriving this period, due next period

info_fields.name: demand_later
info_fields.desc: d_i^(i+2) — arriving this period, due in two periods

info_fields.name: region
info_fields.desc: which of the five fulfilment regimes of eq (18)-(19) fired this period (1-5)

placement.rationale: pure diagnostic; no later transition reads it. Recorded because it makes the piecewise fulfilment auditable in the trajectory and in differential diffs

info_fields.name: action_period
info_fields.desc: period the emitting decision was taken (boundary invariant)

decisions.name: order_quantity

type.rationale: paper section 3 p.719: 'All quantities (e.g., demand, inventory level/position, replenishment order) are assumed to be integers'; integrality also keeps costs strictly comparable with the enumerated DP reference

bounds.rationale: Table 3 at this setting has order-up-to levels 26-36 and reorder points down to -18, so a legitimate single order reaches ~55 units; 60 covers every policy the paper reports, with headroom

decisions.desc: z_i — replenishment quantity ordered at the start of the period (arrives immediately, L=0)

decisions.name: hold_back

type.rationale: same integrality assumption; the protection level is a number of physical units

bounds.rationale: Table 2's most conservative protection level is 11; protection beyond the urgent demand's support does nothing and Poisson(6) essentially never exceeds 15, so 20 is inert headroom

decisions.desc: sigma_i — units of on-hand stock reserved from not-yet-due orders, protecting against next period's urgent arrivals

updates: region = 1 if r0 < 0 else (2 if r1 < 0 else (3 if r2 < 0 else (4 if r2 < need_later else 5)))
inventory = r0 if region == 1 else (0 if region == 2 else (r1 if region == 3 else (hold_back if region == 4 else r1 - need_later)))
due_now = need_next if region == 1 else ((0 - r1) if region == 2 else 0)
due_next = need_later if region <= 3 else ((need_later - r2) if region == 4 else 0)

constants.name: lambda_now
constants.desc: Poisson rate of demand arriving due immediately (paper lambda_0)

constants.name: lambda_next
constants.desc: Poisson rate of demand arriving due next period (lambda_1)

constants.name: lambda_later
constants.desc: Poisson rate of demand arriving due in two periods (lambda_2)

constants.name: fixed_order_cost
constants.desc: K — charged once per period in which anything is ordered

constants.name: holding_cost
constants.desc: h — per unit of positive end-of-period stock

constants.name: backorder_cost
constants.desc: p — per unit of overdue unmet demand, per period

constants.name: supply_leadtime
constants.desc: L — structural in this IR: orders arrive immediately

constants.name: demand_window
constants.desc: T — structural: demand is due within 2 periods, so the profile is (due_now, due_next)

constants.name: discount
constants.desc: alpha — 1.0 throughout the paper's experiments, so total cost is an undiscounted sum

action_modes.name: joint
action_modes.desc: identity: the agent emits (order quantity, hold-back) as one 2-vector; every point in the box is feasible

reward_modes.name: neg_cost
reward_modes.desc: negated per-step cost.total (objective sense is minimize)

requires_memory.rationale: no latent state and no episode-correlated source: at L=0 the whole system state (inventory, due_now, due_next, period) is observable, so the observation is Markov

obs_normalization.rationale: stationary features of heterogeneous magnitude — period 0-12, inventory roughly -60..60, due_now/due_next 0..30

assumptions_log: Supply lead time L=0 is STRUCTURAL in this IR, not a scenario axis: with immediate delivery there is no supply pipeline, so no pipeline state variable exists. Reaching the paper's L=1..4 experiments (Figures 4 and 9) requires re-entering Phase A, not a new instance.

Demand window T=2 is likewise structural: it fixes the advance-demand profile at exactly (due_now, due_next). The homogeneous model of section 3 is recovered as instances exp0 (all mass due immediately, T=0) and exp7 (all mass due in two periods, T=2), per section 4.3.

Why T cannot be a scenario axis without an mdp_ir extension (reviewed and accepted as an envelope boundary): T changes the DECISION DIMENSION, not just constants. Section 4.2 needs one ordering decision plus T-1 protection levels — for T=3, 'protection stock sigma_i^(i+1) covering d_(i+1)^(i+1) and protection stock sigma_i^(i+2) covering d_(i+1)^(i+2)' — so the action space itself would vary per instance. It also changes the demand vector to T+1 components and the advance profile to T entries. Supporting it needs Decision.dim>1 honored by the interpreter (mdp_ir/interpreter.py _random_policy currently emits scalars regardless), per-decision action widths in the gym layer, and the unrolled five-region fulfilment generalized to a cumulative-reserve loop. Note also that the AP dynamic program has state dimension 1+(T-L-1), which is why the paper itself limited its numerics to the two-dimensional case.

The paper never varies T in section 4: 4.3 fixes 'L=0 and T=2', and both the 540- and 810-instance designs sweep L, K, h and p with T held at 2. T only moves in Figure 4's homogeneous study, and those points are reachable inside a T=2 profile as ladder corners. So T=2 costs no fidelity to this source.
Horizon N=12 (the section 4 setting) throughout. The section 3 figures use N=30, so the homogeneous corners here will not reproduce Figure 4's printed costs.

Both decisions are committed at the start of the period, before the demand vector is observed — matching the information set of the paper's own PL heuristics, whose sigma is a constant. The physical timing would allow the hold-back to be chosen after demand arrives (human_confirmed, section 3 event sequence).
Ordering cost is fixed-only (K per ordering period, no variable cost), per section 3: 'we assume that there is only a fixed-order cost and no variable cost'.
Cost components are evaluated at END_OF_PERIOD on end-of-period inventory, i.e. L(x_{i+1}) in eq (5).
Discount alpha=1.0 in every experiment the paper reports, so the objective is a plain sum and the RL discount should be set to 1.0 accordingly.

Terminal convention: the DP recursion ends with C_{N+1}=0, so advance demand arriving near the end of the horizon and due after it is never penalised. Unsatisfied due_now/due_next at the horizon carry no terminal cost.
Initial state (x, v^i, v^{i+1}) = (0, 0, 0), per section 3.3 ('the initial state is (x_1, W_1, V_1) = (0,0,0)').
The three demand components are independent Poisson draws on separate RNG streams (1, 2, 3); a rate of 0 still consumes a draw, so generated code must not short-circuit it.
The delivery-flexibility comparison (the paper's Delta, and its ADI / Gallego-Ozer counterpart) is out of scope for this IR by explicit decision; no exact-delivery dynamics branch exists.
`region` is recorded in info purely to make the piecewise fulfilment of eq (18)-(19) auditable; no transition reads it.
